title: SRE weekly ops sync notes - 2026-03-06
content:
SRE Weekly Ops Sync - 2026-03-06
Owner: Priya Nair
Attendees (planned): Priya, Ethan, Ava, Liam, on-call eng rep
Goals for this sync:
- Quick SLO health check + trends
- Paging summary and root causes for high-frequency pages
- Review top incidents this week and follow-ups
- Action items and owners

TL;DR
- SLOs: overall steady but 3-day elevation in p99 latency for hosted-api routes on 3/3-3/5; error budget for p99 latency down to ~22% for the 30-day window. Availability SLOs still within target but close to threshold for a subset of customers on dedicated clusters.
- Paging: total PD pages this week = 18 (vs 9 baseline); 60% tied to transient infra (node OOM/eviction) and model-serving stalls; remaining due to config regressions in autoscaler.
- Top incidents: RED-4217 (model KV cache eviction bug), RED-4281 (autoscaler misconfig during spike), and a smaller I/O latency blip on Dedicated-3 cluster (no customer-facing impact).

Agenda (30-40m):
1) Quick SLO summary (5m)
2) PagerDuty trends + cause categories (5-7m)
3) Incident deep dive - RED-4217 (10m)
4) Operational mitigations + rollout plan (5m)
5) Review action items + owners (3m)

1) SLO summary
- API success (5xx) SLO: 99.95% target; last 7d = 99.964%; 30d = 99.972% -> healthy.
- p99 inference latency SLO (target < 450ms): 30d window shows 78% error budget remaining historically, but last 7d shows degradation; error budget remaining (30d): ~22% (estimate). Main spike windows: 2026-03-03 10:30-12:00 UTC, 2026-03-04 09:15-10:00 UTC.
- Cache hit-rate SLO for model KV cache: target 85%; last 7d = 76% (drop correlates with RED-4217).
Notes: Need to surface p99 trend to Product so they can delay any risky rollouts until mitigations are in place.

2) Paging trends
- This week: 18 pages. Breakdown: infra/node resource (6), model-serving stalls/KV eviction (7), autoscaler/config regressions (3), postmortem/ops noise (2).
- On-call feedback: most pages are noisy duplicates (same root cause retriggering several PD rules). We should tune PD rules to reduce duplicate pages (thresholding and brief suppression window).
- Suggested short-term: add 5m suppression on chain-triggering alerts for known eviction pattern; longer-term: fix root cause (RED-4217).

3) Incident deep dive: RED-4217 - KV cache eviction bug (reported 2026-03-03)
- Summary: under certain request patterns (long-tail sequences + repeated small-batch concurrency) we observed premature KV cache eviction leading to repeated cold starts and p99 latency spikes.
- Impact: increased p99 latency on hosted-api routes for affected models; small percent of dedicated clusters saw elevated tail latency due to fallback behaviour.
- Root cause (current): race in cache refcounting + subtle GC interaction in the runtime's shard allocator. Patch landed in branch runtime/cache-fix but needs canary.
- Mitigation so far: rolled CPU limit bump on affected pools (reduced evictions) + temporarily increased KV cache size on hot pools (manual). These reduce symptom but not root cause.
- Next steps: schedule canary for runtime/cache-fix in staging -> canary in hosted-prod with 5% traffic, monitor p99 and cache-hit metrics closely (link to RED-4217).

4) RED-4281 - Autoscaler misconfig during traffic spike (summary)
- Summary: an infra config change pushed autoscaler cooldown from 60s to 300s for Dedicated clusters; during a traffic spike autoscaler was slow to add nodes causing queued requests and alerts.
- Fix: rollback config, apply safer default, and add a presubmit guard to prevent cooldown > 120s without approval. Owner: Ethan.

5) Ops/I/O latency blip - Dedicated-3 cluster
- Small I/O degradation for ~20m on 3/4; traced to storage controller firmware flapping; vendor has patch scheduled. No action required other than follow-up with vendor and update cluster-runbook.

Action items (owner, due):
- Priya: Kick off canary for runtime/cache-fix (staging -> 5% prod). Due 2026-03-08. Linked: RED-4217.
- Ethan: Rollback autoscaler change completed; add presubmit guard to infra repo and create a follow-up Jira for presubmit. Due 2026-03-09 (PR + test). Linked: RED-4281.
- Ava: Tune PagerDuty suppression rules for eviction-related alert groups (add 5m suppression). Due 2026-03-07 (make change + monitor).
- Liam: Update Dedicated runbook with vendor storage patch steps and add telemetry dashboard panel for storage health. Due 2026-03-10.
- On-call rotation: add a short note in Slack #oncall about duplicate pages and ask SREs to suppress duplicates while we implement rules. Owner: Priya. Due 2026-03-06 EOD.

Follow-ups for next week
- Post-canary review of runtime/cache-fix metrics (p99, cache-hit-rate, OOMs).
- Evaluate longer-term KV cache redesign options (memory accounting and eviction algorithms) with Applied ML and Serving Runtime teams.
- Run a PD noise reduction retrospective to identify more opportunities for de-dup and threshold tuning.

Notes to self / TODOs (scratchpad)
- Remind product: hold rollouts for model-heavy customers until cache-fix canary passes.
- Check quota impact of temporarily increasing cache sizes for some pools.
- Draft short customer note template in case dedicated customers ask about latency blips.

References / links:
- SLO runbook: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/SRE/SLO+Runbook
- RED-4217: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-4217
- RED-4281: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-4281

Status: draft - will update after canary kickoff and PD rule changes.
